introduction-the-wall-of-yaml.core: Kubernetes apps quickly become thousands of lines of near-duplicate YAML: Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps and Ingresses per service per environment. Helm templating adds string interpolation in whitespace-sensitive YAML, and Kustomize patches have limits. cdk8s defines Kubernetes manifests in TypeScript, Python, Go or Java, with types, loops and classes, and synthesises plain YAML.

first_principles.problem: Changing a label convention means editing 400 YAML files and breaking indentation in Helm templates.
derivation: Use **typed API objects** from k8s schemas.
Output **plain manifests** for any deploy tool.

analogy.title: Printing invitations from a template vs handwriting each
analogy.story: Handwriting 400 cards invites typos; a mail merge from a typed list doesn't.
analogy.breaks: Mail merges are text; cdk8s produces validated API objects.

check.a: Plain Kubernetes YAML manifests, which any tool (kubectl, Argo CD, Flux) can apply.

how-cdk8s-works-a-client-side-rendering-.core: cdk8s runs entirely client-side. Your program builds a construct tree (App → Chart → ApiObjects), `cdk8s synth` walks the tree and writes YAML into dist/, and nothing talks to the cluster. `cdk8s import` generates typed classes from Kubernetes API versions or CRDs, so even custom resources are type-checked. Deployment is a separate step through kubectl or GitOps.

first_principles.problem: Engineers expect cdk8s to deploy like Pulumi and are confused there's no state.
truths: No cluster access needed to synth.

analogy.title: A print shop that only prints
analogy.story: It turns your design into posters; someone else hangs them up.
analogy.breaks: Posters don't reconcile; the cluster controller does.

check.q: Does cdk8s keep state like Terraform or Pulumi?
check.a: No, it only renders YAML; the cluster and your deploy tool own the actual state.

constructs-the-building-blocks-of-cdk8s.core: Like the AWS CDK, cdk8s composes constructs. Low-level ApiObjects map to raw resources, cdk8s-plus provides intent-based L2s (Deployment.exposeViaService, automatic selectors, ConfigMap mounting), and your own constructs package a 'standard microservice' with probes, resources, PDBs and labels. Teams then declare a service in a handful of lines.

first_principles.problem: Every team forgets either readiness probes, resource limits or PodDisruptionBudgets.
derivation: Include **probes, limits, PDB, labels** by default.

analogy.title: A pre-fab house kit
analogy.story: Walls come with wiring and insulation pre-installed; you choose the colour and number of rooms.
analogy.breaks: Kits are fixed; constructs can expose escape hatches.

steps.label: Effect
steps.detail: new StandardService(chart, 'api', { image, port: 8080 }) gives a compliant service.

check.q: What does cdk8s-plus add over raw Kube* objects?
check.a: Intent-based APIs with sensible defaults, like auto-wired selectors and exposeViaService, reducing boilerplate and mistakes.
